rationale: Follows Clojure's MultiFn.java (#30). The tables are mutable fields, as Clojure's are volatile fields, not atoms, and start as empty hash maps, so methods and prefers return hash maps as Clojure's do. -get-method resets the cache when the hierarchy is no longer identical to the one cached (ClojureScript compares with =), and caches a found method only if the tables and hierarchy are unchanged, else it redoes the search. -prefer-method checks for a conflict in the multimethod's hierarchy and returns the multimethod (ClojureScript returns the reset hierarchy). The IFn stanza is unchanged. INamed is dropped, as Clojure's MultiFn is not Named; identity hashing is kept. Messages are Clojure's. Clojure formats each dispatch value with String.format's %s, which calls toString; Suss uses str, with "null" for nil, and pr-str for a value str cannot format, such as a host type. The last dispatch value found in the cache and its method answer the next call with an identical value and an unchanged hierarchy, with no lookup, checked inline in each fixed -invoke arity (#445); every write of the cache forgets the method. An Atom hierarchy's state is read directly, as its -deref answers it, and a keyword dispatch fn is called as the get it is.
